title: COVID-19 Impact on HCP-Pharma Engagement — Veeva/Abelson Taylor Survey 2020
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic fundamentally disrupted HCP-pharma engagement dynamics. A July 2020 survey by Abelson Taylor and Veeva found that 50% of physicians had not seen any sales reps, received tele-details, or e-details in the past week, and 52% stated they would not allow in-person sales rep visits that summer. This catalyzed a permanent shift toward digital and remote engagement channels.

survey_findings.source: Abelson Taylor and Veeva joint survey, July 2020
survey_findings.no_rep_contact: 50% of surveyed physicians had zero sales rep interaction (in-person, telephone, or electronic) in the preceding week
survey_findings.in_person_refusal: 52% of physicians stated they would not allow in-person sales rep visits during the survey period
survey_findings.implications: Demonstrated that traditional in-person detailing was no longer the dominant engagement channel, even temporarily

engagement_shift.pre_covid: In-person detailing was the primary HCP engagement channel. Digital channels were supplementary.
engagement_shift.during_covid: Complete disruption of in-person access. Rapid adoption of video calls, approved email, and digital content sharing.
engagement_shift.post_covid_prediction: Veeva predicted a hybrid model would emerge — reduced but targeted in-person visits combined with sustained digital channel usage. In-person access restrictions expected to persist beyond the pandemic.

my_veeva_for_doctors.description: Veeva launched MyVeeva for Doctors as a unified HCP engagement platform during this period. Intended to give physicians a single portal for managing pharma communications, scheduling, and content access.
my_veeva_for_doctors.strategic_intent: Positioned as the HCP-facing complement to Veeva CRM — if physicians adopt MyVeeva for Doctors as their preferred interface, it deepens Veeva platform lock-in by owning both the rep-side and HCP-side of the engagement.
my_veeva_for_doctors.competitive_relevance: Creates a potential competitive moat. If HCPs prefer receiving communications through MyVeeva for Doctors, switching CRM platforms becomes more disruptive because the HCP-facing channel would need to change.

speaker: David Logue, SVP Commercial Strategy, Veeva Systems
